recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change the 21-Jan open-ended period example to 14-Mar for FHIR-8741; if future readers need more help, handle that as a separate editorial clarification contrasting open-ended periods with point-in-time dates.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive technical correction asking to fix an incorrect date parameter format on the search page and questioning the ge2013-03-14 example that included a period from 21-Jan 2013 onwards.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 7197, represented by Git commit 9ddb75f06e78299173119e7355e1513dea759b23. That commit changed yyyy-mm-ddThh:nn:ss(TZ) to timezone-offset syntax and clarified the 21-Jan open-ended period example while intentionally leaving yyyy-mm-dd and the 21-Jan example in place.
additional_context: The current source/search.html date section uses yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.ssss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm], defines ge as overlap with the inclusive range above the parameter value, and explains that an open-ended period from 21-Jan 2013 may include times after 14-Mar 2013. FHIR-12414 later expanded the same date-prefix examples and preserved that interpretation. A 2024 Zulip thread on the exact example confirmed that an ongoing event starting 21-Jan matches ge2013-03-14, while a point-in-time birthDate of 2013-01-21 would not.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the original typo is fixed and the remaining disputed example is semantically correct under current range-search rules.
